lpz_001: You can recognise it as the female ginkgo, seed coats smelling of rancid butter in autumn where street plantings are usually male. It stands at the corner of Karl-Heine-Strasse.
lpz_002: You can recognise it by its lopsided leaf base and papery, hair-fringed seed, standing directly beside a bald cypress. It stands outside Karl-Heine-Strasse 2.
lpz_003: You can recognise it by its soft, feathery foliage, turning copper and dropping entirely for winter unlike an evergreen conifer. It stands beside the elm outside Karl-Heine-Strasse 2.
lpz_004: You can recognise it by its near-black foliage and smooth grey bark, a few doors from the street's Japanese pagoda tree. It stands at Karl-Heine-Strasse 24.
lpz_005: You can recognise it by flowering in August, creamy white clusters when most other street trees have finished for the year. It stands at Karl-Heine-Strasse 24b.
lpz_006: You can recognise it by leaves so deeply cut and narrow they barely register as beech foliage at all. It stands behind the fence of a former villa on Karl-Tauchnitz-Strasse.
lpz_007: You can recognise it by its acorns carried clear of the twig on a short stalk, unlike the stalkless acorns of a sessile oak. It stands behind a villa garden wall on Kaethe-Kollwitz-Strasse.
